correctness.rationale: Unique difference intervals follow from the published Type-A lemma. Intersecting two intervals for incident edges forces a common two-symbol alphabet, so the opposite edge has symmetric-difference support. The only allowed interval geometries yield one unique adjacent pivot. Its equal-symbol boundary is necessary and sufficient. Counting its ordered first-symbol pair, block split, interval location and outside context gives T exactly. Independent deletion-set enumeration and pivot checks corroborate all cases q=2 n<=11, q=3 n<=7, q=4 n<=6; the proof, not the finite checks, is all-length.
